about: Examples for one number: today's target in MET-hours, the 2.1 in "0.0/2.1" on the Today page.
The app and the backend each have their own copy of this calculation:
src/lib/met.ts and src/lib/plan.ts in the app, backend/app/calculator.py in the backend.
Two tests read this file and work every example out, one with each copy:
Both have to get `today_target`, to 3 decimals. The answers were worked out by hand; `how` shows the arithmetic.
When a rule changes on purpose: change both copies, then the answers here.

fields.plan: the 7 days, Monday first, each one of: off | 0 | 5 | 10 | 30 | 45 (minutes)
fields.workouts: this week's workouts: day (0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday), met, minutes. A workout from Fitbit also has its Fitbit band (fairly | very) and whether the user confirmed it; one without `confirmed` is confirmed.

examples.name: Monday, nothing done yet this week
examples.how: The week has 105 planned minutes and Monday has 30 of them: 7.5 × 30 / 105

examples.name: Wednesday, one workout on Monday
examples.how: Monday earned 5 × 30 / 60 = 2.5, so 5.0 is left. Wednesday and Saturday have 75 minutes, Wednesday 30 of them: 5.0 × 30 / 75

examples.name: Light activity does not count, and 3 MET is where counting starts
examples.how: The 2 MET workout earns nothing. The 3 MET one earns 3 × 20 / 60 = 1.0, so 6.5 is left: 6.5 × 30 / 75

examples.name: Fitbit workouts nobody confirmed count at the bottom of their band
examples.how: Monday counts at 3.0 MET (fairly): 3.0 × 40 / 60 = 2.0. Tuesday counts at 6.0 MET (very): 6.0 × 30 / 60 = 3.0. 2.5 is left: 2.5 × 30 / 75

examples.name: The same Fitbit workouts, confirmed, count at their own MET
examples.how: Monday earned 4.5 × 40 / 60 = 3.0 and Tuesday 6.8 × 30 / 60 = 3.4. 1.1 is left: 1.1 × 30 / 75

examples.name: Today is a day off
examples.how: Tuesday is off in the plan, so it has no target

examples.name: A workout today does not move today's target
examples.how: The target is set at the start of the day, when 5.0 was left: 5.0 × 30 / 75. Today's own 1.0 does not change it

examples.name: The week's goal is already reached
examples.how: Monday earned 8 × 60 / 60 = 8.0, more than 7.5, so nothing is left

examples.name: Today is the last planned day of the week
examples.how: Monday earned 2.5 and Wednesday 4 × 30 / 60 = 2.0, so 3.0 is left. Saturday has all 45 of the minutes still planned: 3.0 × 45 / 45

examples.name: Another plan, with 0, 5 and 10 minute days
examples.how: Tuesday to Sunday have 10 + 30 + 5 + 45 = 90 minutes, Tuesday 10 of them: 7.5 × 10 / 90
